page: Amazon Web Services is4gen.xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton series processors. It provides 4 dedicated physical cores built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture operating at 2.5 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 24.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:6 ratio of 6.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs present. For storage, the instance incorporates a high-density 3,750 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark results demonstrate a profile skewed heavily toward storage and data handling rather than intensive computation. Multi-core and single-core stress-ng tests place the processor in the middle 50% tier (scores of 6055.17 and 1519.48, respectively). Similarly, large-block memory bandwidth sustains average throughput, registering 73.07 GB/sec on uncached reads and 35.12 GB/sec on writes. However, compute-heavy and vector tasks score predominantly in the lower quartile, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3226.0, single-core score of 961.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 2699.24. Compression performance is modest, reaching 20.28 GB/sec in gzip and 23.98 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the is4gen.xlarge optimizes density by pairing power-efficient Arm cores with an expansive 3.75 TB local NVMe volume. It does not excel at raw mathematical compute, static web serving throughput (4.86 GB/sec), or LLM inference (26.69 tokens/sec generation on 135M models). Instead, it delivers its greatest efficiency in I/O-heavy environments where low-latency local storage capacity matters more than raw compute, such as distributed log processing, cache nodes, and local data stores.
description: Amazon Web Services is4gen.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an ARMv8 AWS Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores at 2.5 GHz, 24.0 GB of RAM (6.0 GB per core), 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and zero GPUs. A central attribute is its integrated 3,750 GB local NVMe SSD, designed for high-density storage applications. Benchmark metrics indicate mid-range integer and multi-core processing (stress-ng multi-core 6055.17) alongside solid uncached memory throughput (73.07 GB/sec read, 35.12 GB/sec write). However, computational workloads like Geekbench (3226.0 multi-core) and LLM token generation fall within lower percentiles. The instance provides strong resource density for disk-intensive workloads, making it well matched for distributed databases, local caching tiers, log search systems, and ETL pipelines requiring large local non-volatile storage.
